title: Lower-cut realization of a supplied chronological maximum history
statement: Let $V$ be totally ordered with least element, $\nu$ a supplied resolution invariant calculus [def-trf-resolution-invariant-calculus-data], and $A$ an embedded rational pair. Given a stopped chronological maximum history $S$ of length $r$, with all its prefixes, positive strictly increasing reverse-order labels, center and intermediate geometry [lem-trf-maximum-history-chronology], there is a finite labeled embedded resolution tower [def-trf-labeled-embedded-resolution] on $L=(V\setminus\{\bot\})^{\mathrm{op}}$ with active labels exactly those of $S$. Its monotone cut index is the number of chronological labels in the cut. The empty and full cuts give $0$ and $r$; the strict and weak principal cuts at label $l_i$ give $i$ and $i+1$. Its ambient and intrinsic diagrams identify naturally with the final history of $S$ reindexed by this map, compatibly with inclusion and the initial identifications. The ambient center at each active label and its intrinsic kernel are the corresponding final-history ideals pulled back through these identifications. At an inactive label the strict and weak principal cuts have equal index. These data form MaximumHistoryCutTower S. The finite stopped history is supplied as a hypothesis; neither its existence nor uniqueness of its length is asserted here.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.1.1--2.1.4 and 2.3.4--2.3.5, printed pp.86--87,91--92; explicit lower-cut construction in original finite-realization Steps 5--6

proof.text: For each lower set D count the indices whose strictly increasing label lies in D. Lower closure makes them a prefix. Inclusion of cuts increases its size, and strict increase computes the sizes at bottom, top and both principal cuts. This is the desired monotone finite index.

Compose successive Extension isomorphisms to identify each prefix with the corresponding portion of the final history. Reindex the final ambient and intrinsic diagrams by the opposite cut-index functor. At active labels transport the recorded center ideals and ordinary blowup/strict-transform isomorphisms. Naturality, initial normalizations, all center equations and coherence follow from these prefix identifications.

At an inactive label use the unit ideal and the map from its empty subscheme to the intrinsic scheme. Its intrinsic kernel is also the unit ideal, so both ideals are coherent. The cut index is constant there, so transitions are identities; the invertible-center theorem identifies the unit-ideal ordinary blowup with the original scheme, and the strict transform is the original scheme because the complementary open is the whole scheme. Intervals with no active labels likewise have constant index. Final regularity and the nonregular earlier prefixes imply stopAtRegular; the length-zero input clauses give empty and regular inputs. Every active center remains recorded.
